senses: novae rēs, meaning a new or different state, etc.: an idiom for a revolution
la:noun:res.html:
rēs, rei (rēi with e long;
gen., ; ; ; dat., ; ; rei, gen., monosyl. at the end of the verse, ; and in the middle of the verse,, and Poët. ap. ), f.
etym. dub.; perh. root ra- of reor, ratus; cf. Germ. Ding; Engl. thing, from denken, to think; prop., that which is thought of; cf. also λόγος, Lid. and Scott, 9
, a thing, object, being; a matter, affair, event, fact, circumstance, occurrence, deed, condition, case, etc.; and sometimes merely = something (cf.: causa, ratio, negotium).
In gen.: unde initum primum capiat res quaeque movendi,; cf. : in partes res quaeque minutas Distrahitur,: summe Sol, qui omnes res inspicis, Enn. ap. Prob. (Trag. v. 321 Vahl.): versus, quos ego de Rerum Naturā pangere conor,; cf. ; : rerum natura creatrix,: divinarum humanarumque rerum, tum initiorum causarumque cujusque rei cognitio, (v. divinus): haeret haec res,: profecto, ut loquor, ita res est,: haud mentior, resque uti facta dico,: de Alcumenā ut rem teneatis rectius, prol. 110: in tantis rebus (sc. in re publicā defendendā), et saep.: quo Averna vocantur nomine, id ab re Impositum est, quia sunt avibus contraria cunctis,from the nature of the thing,; cf. ; : si res postulabit,the condition of the case,: scaena rei totius haec, Cael. ap. : fugam in se nemo convertitur Nec recedit loco, quin statim rem gerat,does his duty, stands his ground,; so, res gerere, v. gero; hence, too, rerum scriptor, for a historian, v. scriptor, and cf. II. H. infra.—
With adj. of quality, to express condition, etc.: illic homo a me sibi malam rem arcessit,is bringing a bad business on himself,; so, res mala,a wretched condition,; and more freq. in plur.: bonis tuis rebus meas res irrides malas,circumstances, condition,; : res secundae,good fortune,; cf. : res prosperae,; : in secundissimis rebus,: adversae res,; ; : res belli adversae,: res dubiae,; ; ; ; v. bonus, florens, salvus, adversus, dubius, novus, arduus, etc.— Freq. in curses, etc.: in malam rem,go to the bad,; : malam rem hinc ibis?.—
With an adj. in a periphrasis: abhorrens ab re uxoriā,matrimony,: in arbitrio rei uxoriae,dowry,: rem divinam nisi compitalibus ... ne faciat,a religious act, act of worship, a sacrifice,: bellicam rem administrari majores nostri nisi auspicato noluerunt,; : erat ei pecuaria res ampla et rustica,: res rustica, agriculture: rei rusticae libro primo,; , praef. § 19: liber, quem de rebus rusticis scripsi,: navalis rei certamina,naval battles,: res militaris,: rei militaris gloria,; : res frumentaria,forage,; ; : armatae rei scientissimus,: peritus aquariae rei,: res judicaria,: res ludicra,play,: uti rebus veneriis,; : res Veneris,; ; v. also familiaris, judiciaria, militaris, navalis, etc., and cf. II. G. infra. —
With pronouns or adjectives, as an emphatic periphrase for the neutr.: ibi me inclamat Alcumena: jam ea res me horrore afficit,this now,; cf.: De. Estne hoc, ut dico? Li. Rectam instas viam: Ea res est,it is even so,: de fratre confido ita esse ut semper volui. Multa signa sunt ejus rei,of it,: quos (μελιττῶνας) alii μελιττοτροφεῖα appellant, eandem rem quidam mellaria. : sunt ex te quae scitari volo, Quarum rerum, etc.,; cf. : quibus de rebus quoniam nobis contigit ut aliquid essemus consecuti,: quā super re interfectum esse Hippotem dixisti? Pac. ap. Fest. s. v. superescit, p. 244: resciscet Amphitruo rem omnem,every thing, all,: nulla res tam delirantes homines concinat cito,nothing,; cf.: neque est ulla res, in quā, etc.,; ; cf. also: sumptu ne parcas ullā in re, quod ad valetudinem opus sit,: magna res principio statim bello,a great thing, a great advantage,: nil admirari prope res est una Solaque, quae, etc.,the only thing, only means, et saep. — Emphatically with sup.: scilicet rerum facta est pulcherrima Roma,the most beautiful thing in the world,; Spald. p. 81. — Of persons, etc.: est genus hominum, qui esse primos se omnium rerum volunt,: maxime rerum,; cf.: maxima rerum Roma,; : fortissima rerum animalia,: pulcherrime rerum,; ; : dulcissime rerum,.—
In adverb. phrases: e re natā melius fieri haud potuit,after what has happened,: pro re natā,according to circumstances,; : pro tempore et pro re,: factis benignus pro re,according to circumstances,; : pro re pauca loquar,; : ex re et ex tempore,: e re respondi,.
In partic.
Pregn., an actual thing, the thing itself, reality, truth, fact; opposed to appearance, mere talk, the mere name of a thing: ecastor, re experior, quanti facias uxorem tuam,: desiste dictis nunc jam miseram me consolari: Nisi quid re praesidium apparas, etc.,: rem ipsam loqui. : rem fabulari,: nihil est aliud in re,in fact, Weissenb. ad loc.: se ipsa res aperit,: ex re decerpere fructus,; opp. verbum, vox, opinio, spes, nomen, etc.: rem opinor spectari oportere, non verba,; cf.: te rogo, ut rem potiorem oratione ducas, Matius ap. : non modo res omnes, sed etiam rumores cognoscamus,: qui hos deos non re, sed opinione esse dicunt,: Peripateticos et Academicos nominibus differentes, re congruentes,: quod nos honestum, illi vanum ... verbis quam re probabilius vocant,; : eum, tametsi verbo non audeat, tamen re ipsā de maleficio suo confiteri,; cf. : vides quantum distet argumentatio tua ab re ipsā atque a veritate,. — Hence, abl. sing., often strengthened by verā (sometimes as one word, reverā), in fact, really, in truth, indeed, in reality: haec ille, si verbis non audet, re quidem verā palam loquitur,; so, re quidem verā,; : re autem verā,; and simply re verā,; ; : re verāque,; cf.: et re verā,indeed, in fact,; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; , ext. 1; ; ; .—
Effects, substance, property, possessions: mihi Chrysalus Perdidit filium, me atque rem omnem Meam,; cf.: Ph. Habuitne rem? Ly. Habuit. Ph. Qui eam perdidit ... Mercaturamne an venales habuit, ubi rem perdidit? : quibus et re salvā et perditā profueram,: rem talentum decem,; : avidior ad rem,: rem facere,to make money,: res eos jampridem, fides deficere nuper coepit,,

10: qui duo patrimonia accepisset remque praeterea bonis et honestis rationibus auxisset,: libertino natum patre et in tenui re,in narrow circumstances, et saep.; v. also familiaris.— In plur.: quantis opibus, quibus de rebus, Enn. ap. (Trag. v. 396 Vahl.): privatae res,.—

Hence, law t. t., whatever may be the subject of a right, whether corporeal or incorporeal (v. Sandars, Introd. to p. 42 sqq.): res corporales,; ; : res in patrimonio, res extra patrimonium, pr.; : res sanctae,; v. also mancipium, privatus, etc.—
Benefit, profit, advantage, interest, weal: res magis quaeritur, quam, etc.,: melius illi consulas quam rei tuae,: haec tuā re feceris,to your advantage,.— Most freq. with the prepositions in, ex, ob, ab, etc.: quasi istic minor mea res agatur quam tua,is interested, affected, (v. ago): si in rem tuam esse videatur,: vide si hoc in rem deputas,: quod in rem recte conducat tuam,: si in remst utrique,: quid mihi melius est, quid magis in rem est, quam? etc.,useful,: tamen in rem fore credens universos adpellare,: omnia quae in rem videbantur esse,: ad conparanda ea quae in rem erant,: imperat quae in rem sunt,; : ex tuā re non est, ut ego emoriar,for your advantage,: An. Non pudet Vanitatis? Do. Minime, dum ob rem, to the purpose, with advantage, : ob rem facere, usefully, with advantage or profit, : subdole blanditur, ab re Consulit blandiloquentulus, contrary to his interest, i. e. to his injury, Brix ad loc.: haud id est ab re aucupis,: haec haud ab re duxi referre,: non ab re esse Quinctio visum est interesse, etc.,; ; ; ; ; .—
Cause, reason, ground, account; only in the connection eā (hac) re, and eam ob rem, adverb., therefore, on that account: eā re tot res sunt, ubi bene deicias,: hac re nequeunt ex omnibus omnia gigni, Quod, etc.,; cf.: illud eā re a se esse concessum, quod, etc.,: patrem exoravi, tibi ne noceat, neu quid ob eam rem succenseat,; cf.: quoi rei?for what purpose?; .—Hence (by uniting into one word) the causal adverbs quare and quamobrem, v. h. vv.—
An affair, matter of business, business: cum et de societate inter se multa communicarent et de totā illā ratione atque re Gallicanā,: rem cum aliquo transigere,. — Hence, transf., in gen.: res alicui est cum aliquo,to have to do with any one,; ; ; ; cf.: famigeratori res sit cum damno et malo, Brix ad loc.— Also without a dat.: quoniam cum senatore res est,; esp., in mal. part.: rem habere cum aliquo or aliquā,to have to do with any one,; ; ; . —Ellipt.: jam biennium est, quom mecum rem coepit,. —
A case in law, a lawsuit, cause, suit (more gen. than causa): ubi res prolatae sunt,: res agi,; : quibus res erat in controversiā, ea vocabatur lis,; cf. (prob. in allusion to this legal form): tot homines ... statuere non potuisse, utrum diem tertium an perendinum ... rem an litem dici oporteret,; cf. also: quarum rerum litium causarum condixit pater patratus, etc., an ancient formula,: de rebus ab aliquo cognitis judicatisque dicere,: pecunias capere ob rem judicandam,: si res certabitur olim,; ; ; : tractu temporis futurum, ut res pereat,: rem differre,: res judicata dicitur, quae finem controversiarum pronuntiatione judicis accipit, et saep.—
An affair, esp. a battle, campaign, military operations; in phrase rem (or res) gerere: res gesta virtute,: ut res gesta est ordine narrare,: his rebus gestis,: res gerere,: rem bene gerere,; : comminus rem gerunt,: res gestae,; : adversus duos simul rem gerere,: rem male gerere,; : in relatione rerum ab Scythis gestarum,; cf.: rem agere,; : ante rem,before the battle,: cum Thebanis sibi rem esse existimant,; .—
Acts, events, as the subject of narration, a story, history: res in unam sententiam scripta,: cui lecta potenter erit res,; ; : in medias res auditorem rapere,; : agitur res in scaenis,; cf.: numeros animosque secutus, non res,; : sicut in rebus ejus (Neronis) exposuimus,: litterae, quibus non modo res omnis, sed etiam rumores cognoscamus,: res populi Romani perscribere, Liv. praef. § 1: res Persicae,history,; .—
Res publica, also as one word, respublica, the common weal, a commonwealth, state, republic (cf. civitas); also, civil affairs, administration, or power, etc.: qui pro republicā, non pro suā obsonat, Cato ap. ; cf.: erat tuae virtutis, in minimis tuas res ponere, de re publicā vehementius laborare,: dummodo ista privata sit calamitas et a rei publicae periculis sejungatur,; cf.: si re publicā non possis frui, stultum est nolle privatā,: egestates tot egentissimorum hominum nec privatas posse res nec rem publicam sustinere, (v. publicus); Cato ap. : auguratum est, rem Romanam publicam summam fore, Att. ap. : quo utiliores rebus suis publicis essent,: commutata ratio est rei totius publicae,: pro republicā niti, Cato ap. : merere de republicā,: de re publicā disputatio . . . dubitationem ad rem publicam adeundi tollere, etc.,: oppugnare rem publicam,; ; : paene victā re publicā,: delere rem publicam,; .—Esp. in the phrase e re publicā, for the good of the State, for the public benefit: senatūs consultis bene et e re publicā factis,: ea si dicam non esse e re publicā dividi,; ; ; ; ; —Post-class. and rare, also ex republicā, ; ; but exque is used for euphony (class.): id eum recte atque ordine exque re publicā fecisse,; ; .— In plur.: eae nationes respublicas suas amiserunt, C. Gracch. ap. Fest. s. h. v. p. 286 Müll.: hoc loquor de tribus his generibus rerum publicarum,: circuitus in rebus publicis commutationum, et saep.—
Sometimes simply res, the State (in the poets, and since the Aug. per. in prose): unus homo nobis cunctando restituit rem, Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 313 Vahl.): hic (Marcellus) rem Romanam sistet,; cf.: nec rem Romanam tam desidem umquam fuisse,; : parva ista non contemnendo majores nostri maximam hanc rem fecerunt,: Romana,; ; ; ; cf.: ut paulo ante animum inter Fidenatem Romanamque rem ancipitem gessisti,: Albana,.— In plur.: res Asiae evertere,: custode rerum Caesare,; cf.: res sine discordiā translatae,; so (also in Cic.), rerum potiri, v. potior. —
Res novae, political changes, a revolution, etc.; v. novus.

la:verb:restituo.html:
rē-stĭtŭo, ŭi, ūtum, 3, v. a.
statuo
,
to put or set up again, i. e. either to replace in its former position, or (more freq.) to restore to its former condition, to rebuild, revive, etc. (freq. and class.; syn.: restauro, renovo, reficio).
In gen.
Lit.: senatus decrevit, ut Minerva nostra, quam turbo dejecerat, restitueretur,, a, 1: arborem,: luxatum femur ex toto,: aedes (with reficere), : domum a Clodio disjectam,i. e. to rebuild,; cf. domum,: theatrum,: statuas (disjectas),: tropaea disjecta,: fores effractas,: oppida vicosque, quos incenderant,: fontes et Flumina,: turbatas comas,: ordines,; cf. aciem,; : inclinatam aciem,: (eos, qui) quaedam contra naturam depravata habent, restituere et corrigere,: oculos (luminibus orbati),: visum,: pilos,: se (apes, with reviviscere),; cf.: aliquem a limine mortis,; ; and restinctos,to raise the dead,: apes restituunt se ac reviviscunt,.—
Trop., to restore, revive, renew, reform, etc.: unus homo nobis cunctando restituit rem, Enn. ap. ; ; ; Serv.; ; ; Aug. ap. (Ann. v. 313 Vahl.); cf.: rem prolapsam,: res perditas,; : rem impeditam et perditam,; and simply rem, Drak.; 8, 11; 25, 37: veteres clientelas,: veterem tuam illam calliditatem atque prudentiam,: tribuniciam potestatem,: tribuniciam intercessionem armis,: proelium, Poet. ap. ; ; ; ; cf.: pugnam omnibus locis,; : damna Romano accepta bello,: sanitatem,: bellum,; ; cf. vires,: adulescentem corruptum,to reform,: suorum a pudore maritimae ignominiae restituti animi,restored, revived,: consolando aliquorum restituere voluntatem aut benevolentiam in dominum,.—
In partic., to give back, deliver up, return, restore a thing belonging to a person or place (syn. reddo).
Lit.: Mi. Paterna oportet reddi filio bona. Ha. Restituentur omnia, : tribuni vobis amissa reddent ac restituent?.— With a personal object: virginem suis Restituere ac reddere,; : alicui filium,; ; : amissa cuique,: bona iis,: majorum locum huic,: agrum Veientibus, et saep.: alicui suum familiarem et hospitem, ereptum e manibus hostium,: Sextus Pompeius civitati restitutus,: captum victori,: apibus fructum suum,: Caesaris imperio restituendus erat,: illum restituam huic, hic autem in Alidem me meo patri,: aliquem natalibus,to set free,; v. natalis.— With abstr. object: sed etiam meam vocem et auctoritatem et vobis et rei publicae conservatam ac restitutam puto,: lucem salutemque redditam sibi ac restitutam,.—Without dat.: amissa (opp. adimere),: fraudata,fin. al.: Arpi restituti ad Romanos,; cf.: (Cloelia) sospites omnes Romam ad propinquos restituit,; : aliquem in aliquem locum,; cf. : (Siciliam) in antiquum statum,; cf.: civitates afflictas in melius,. —
Publicists' and jurid. t. t., to bring back or restore to his previous state or condition; to recall, reinstate a person condemned, banished, deprived of his property, etc. (cf. reduco): restituebat multos calamitosos ... Licinium Denticulam de aleā condemnatum restituit,: omnes, qui lege Pompeiā condemnati essent,: quae fuisset justa causa restituendi mei, nisi fuisset injusta eiciendi?; cf. : aliquem (damnatum),; : exsulem,: legionem totam cum ignominiā missam,: neque enim praetor, si ex eo fundo essem dejectus, ita me restitui jussit,; cf. : nonnullos ambitus Pompeiā lege damnatos in integrum restituit, Caes. B. C. 3, 1: aliquem in integrum,; ; (cf. the whole section, : De in integrum restitutionibus); cf.: Sampsiceramum restitui in eum locum cupere, ex quo decidit,: equites Romanos in tribunicium honorem,: tribunos plebis in suam dignitatem,: restitutus in patriam (Camillus) patriam ipsam restituit,; so, in patriam,.—
Transf.
Of things, to deliver up again, to make restitution of, restore: in utriusque bonis nihil erat, quod restitui posset, nisi quod moveri loco non poterat,; ; —
Of a previous judicial sentence or of injustice committed, to reverse, i. e. to make null and void, to make good again, repair (cf.: rescindo, resolvo): alia judicia Lilybaei, alia Agrigenti, alia Panhormi restituta sunt,: qui (praetor) dies totos aut vim fieri vetat aut restitui factam jubet, etc.,: ut si ego eum condemnaro, tu restituas,; cf.: restitui in integrum aequom est,.—
To compensate for, make good (rare): damnum,; : jacturam,. —
Trop., to restore to a former condition, to re-establish, etc.: ut anno XVI. post reges exactos secederent, leges sacratas ipsi sibi restituerent,restored for themselves, re-established,, Fragm. 23, p. 450 fin. Orell.: restituit his animos parva una res,; cf. : ut interfecto Punico praesidio restituerent se Romanis,join themselves again to the Romans,: ulcera sanitati restituens,restoring,; cf. : Bacchus peccasse fatentem Restituit,restored to his former condition,; cf.: cum semel occideris ... Non, Torquate, genus, non te facundia, non te Restituet pietas,: restituam jam ego te in gaudia,: haud facile te in eundem rursus restitues locum,; ; cf.: cives ex servitute in libertatem,: poëtam in locum, prol. alt. 13: aliquem rursus in gratiam,; cf.: fratrem in antiquum locum gratiae et honoris,: fratrem (sc. in gratiam),: Acarnanas in antiquam formulam jurisque ac dicionis eorum,: vos in amicitiam societatemque nostram, et saep.: cum praecipitata raptim consilia neque revocari neque in integrum restitui possint,: patientiae veteri (Britanniam),.

la:verb:rescindo.gloss: to cut off, cut or break down or back, cut or tear open or loose
senses: to cut off, cut or break down or back, cut or tear open or loose
to annul, abolish, abrogate, cancel, revoke, repeal, rescind
la:verb:rescindo.html:
rē-scindo, scĭdi, scissum, 3, v. a.,
to cut off, cut loose, cut or break down; to cut or tear open (freq. and class.).
Lit.: pontem,i. e. to break down,; fin.; 6, 29; 7, 35; 7, 58 fin.; ; ; : vallum ac loricam falcibus,: pluteos, ap. : cameras tectorum,: tecta domusque in usum novae classis,: caelum,; : tenuem vestem e membris,: vestes,: decreta,: ense teli latebram penitus,to cut open,: vulnera,; ; : pectora ferro,: rescisso palato,: plagam,: venam,to open,; ; and poet.: obductos annis luctus,: an male sarta Gratia nequidquam coit et rescinditur?; imitated by Petronius: ne inter initia coëuntis gratiae recentem cicatricem rescinderet,.—
Meton., to open: vias,: locum praesidiis firmatum atque omni ratione obvallatum,: ferro summum Ulceris os,; ; cf.: latentia vitia (corresp. to aperire),.—
Trop., to annul, abolish, abrogate, repeal, rescind a law, decree, agreement, etc.: mihi non videtur, quod sit factum legibus, Rescindi posse,: acta M. Antonii rescidistis, leges refixistis,; so, acta,; 13, 3, 5; ; ; ; : acta deūm,: jussa Jovis,: constitutiones senatūs,: concilia habita,: totam triennii praeturam,: rescindere et irritas facere omnes istius injurias,, § 63: res judicatas,; cf. judicium,: judicia,: ambitiosas Centumvir. sententias,: pactiones,: testamenta mortuorum,; ; : foedus turpe,.— Poet.: aevi leges validas,: beneficium suum insequenti injuriā,: verbum Dei,.

senses: to offer or present in return
to be present, to appear, attend
to meet, agree, accord or correspond with, conform to, answer for
la:verb:respondeo.html:
rē-spondĕo, di, sum, 2, v. a.
Lit., to promise a thing in return for something else; to offer or present in return. So, only in a few examples, the phrase par pari (dat.) respondere, to return like for like: par pari respondes dicto, you return tit for tat with your tongue (syn. refero), ; cf.: istuc serva; et verbum verbo par pari ut respondeas, Ter Phorm. 1, 4, 35; and: paria paribus respondimus,.— Pass.: provide, si cui quid debetur, ut sit, unde par pari respondeatur, i. e. that there be wherewithal to meet the demand, Atticus ap. ; cf. also under II. A. 1, the lusus verbb. with spondeo; and II. B. init.—
In a more general signification.
To answer, reply, respond (either to a question, or to any statement or remark, and either in a friendly or hostile signif.); constr. aliquid alicui, ad, adversus, contra aliquem (aliquid).
In gen.
Lit.: Th. Aliud te rogo. Tr. Aliud ergo nunc tibi respondeo, ; cf. .—Absol.: prius respondes, quam rogo,: eā legatione Papirius auditā ... respondit,; ; ; : ille appellatus respondit,; ; ; ; ; ; ; 9, 14, 2. — So usu. of an oral answer: tibi non rescribam, sed respondeam,; but also of writing: epistulae, et saep.; v.infra: ab his sermo oritur, respondet Laelius,; : olli respondit rex Albaï Longaï, Enn. ap. P. (Ann. v. 34 Vahl.): cui orationi Caepionis ore respondit Aelius,: criminibus,: supremae tuae paginae,: cui opinioni,: tam aequae postulationi,: summā constantiā ad ea, quae quaesita erant, respondebat,; cf.: arbitrabar me satis respondisse ad id quod quaesierat Laelius,: nec absurde adversus utrosque respondisse visus est,; : adversus haec imperator respondit,; fin.— With acc. of neutr. pron.: illud respondere cogam,to make answer to that,; cf. ; : multa contra patronos venuste testis saepe respondet,; ; cf.: accipe, quid contra juvenis responderit,.— With object-clause: respondent, bello se et suos tutari posse,; ; ; . 102 al. —Introducing a direct answer: cum dixisset, Quid agis, Grani? respondit, Immo vero tu, Druse, quid agis!; id. ; ; .— In impers. perf.: postquam mihi responsum est, abeo, etc.,; cf. : quid nunc renunciem abs te responsum? : sic existimet: Responsum non dictum esse, quia laesit prior,.— In plur.: multa ejus et in senatu et in foro vel provisa prudenter vel acta constanter vel responsa acute ferebantur,.— In the sup.: (haec) quam brevia responsu,— In a lusus verbb. with spondeo: Er. Sponden' tu istud? He. Spondeo. Er. At ego, tuum tibi advenisse filium, respondeo, and in return I promise you, i. e. assure you, ; cf.: fideiussores, qui salvam rempublicam fore responderunt, etc.,promised, gave assurance,—
Trop., to answer, respond, reply to, re-echo, resound, etc.: saxa et solitudines voci respondent,; respondent flebile ripae,; and: respondentia tympana,: urbes coloniarum respondebunt Catilinae tumulis silvestribus, will give an answer to, i. e. will prove a match for, .—
In partic.
Of lawyers, priests, oracles, etc., to give an opinion, advice, decision, response: quaeris, num juris consultus (sit)? quasi quisquam sit, qui sibi hunc falsum de jure respondisse dicat,; so, de jure,; cf.: de jure consulentibus respondere,; in a like signif., also simply jus,: facultas respondendi juris,; ; ; cf.: civica jura,; and: quae consuluntur, minimo periculo respondentur, etc.,; . —Absol., ; and so very freq. of the jurists in the Digests; v. responsum: pater Roscii ad haruspices retulit: qui responderunt, nihil illo puero clarius fore,: cum ex prodigiis haruspices respondissent,; ; ; ; : responsum est,: deliberantibus Pythia respondit, ut moenibus ligneis se munirent,gave advice,; cf. : possumus seniores amici quiete respondere,to give advice,—
Of the answering of a person summoned when his name is called; hence, meton., to appear: citatus neque respondit neque excusatus est, Varr. ap. ; cf.: cives, qui ad nomina non respondissent,: quia Romae non respondebant,; ; ; ; (vadato, dat., i.e. ei qui eum vadatus erat; v. vador); ; et saep.—
Esp., to appear before a tribunal, to answer an accusation, meet a charge, etc.: perfectus in exsilium Tubulus est nec respondere ausus,: Verrem alterā actione responsurum non esse,: nemo Epaminondam responsurum putabat,.—
Transf., in gen., to appear, be present: ipsi (sc. paeon et herous) se offerent et respondebunt non vocati,: verba (with res se ostendent),: ut ii, qui debent, non respondeant ad tempus,; cf.: podagra ad tempus (with venit ad horam),: sanguis per menstrua,.—
To answer to; to meet, agree, accord, or correspond with a thing; constr. usually with dat. or absol.: ut omnia omnibus paribus paria respondeant,: ut horum auctoritatibus illorum orationi, qui dissentiunt, respondere posse videamur,: ut verba verbis quasi demensa et paria respondeant,; and: respondent extrema primis, media utrisque, omnia omnibus,: (Aristoteles dicit) illam artem (sc. rhetoricam) quasi ex alterā parte respondere dialecticae, that it corresponds to, i. e. forms the counterpart of, : aedificare alteram porticum quae Palatio responderet,; cf. of a locality: contra elata mari respondet Gnosia tellus,i. e. lies opposite,: Pachyni pulsata Ionio respondent saxa profundo,: est mihi magnae curae, ut ita erudiatur (Lucullus), ut et patri et Caepioni nostro et tibi tam propinquo respondeat,: satis Graecorum

gloriae responderunt, : tua virtus opinioni hominum,; : fortuna meis optatis,; cf.: seges votis,: arma Caesaris non responsura lacertis,: favor meritis,: ne prior officio quisquam respondeat,: par fama labori,: fructus labori,: non mihi respondent veteres in carmine vires,: familiam nemo speciosiorem producet, sed hominibus non respondet,he does not pay his debts,: amori amore respondere,i. e. to return it, repay it,; cf.: Quinti fratris liberalitati subsidiis amicorum,: qui ex vico ortus est, eam patriam intellegitur habere, cui reipublicae vicus ille respondet,to which it belongs,.— In mal. part.: mulieribus,.—With ad: respondere ad parentum speciem,resemble,: deformentur directiones, ut longitudines ad regulam et lineam, altitudines ad perpendiculum, anguli ad normam respondentes exigantur,; cf.: structuram ad perpendiculum respondere oportet,: quia non tota ad animum responderat (villa),: ad spem eventus respondit,.—With dat.: Papirio quoque brevi ad spem eventus respondit,.— With ex: quicquid non ex voluntate respondet, iram provocat,: speculum quocumque obvertimus oris, Res sibi respondent simili formā atque colore,i. e. correspond, are reflected,.— Absol.: sidera respondent in aquā,: quia raro verba belle respondeant,: medicus aliquid oportet inveniat, quod non ubique fortasse, sed saepius tamen etiam respondeat, may answer, be suitable, Cels. praef.—

To return, make a return, yield: frumenta quando cum quarto responderint (sc. colono),have returned, yielded,; cf. with abl. and dat.: humus cum est repetita cultu, magno fenore colono respondet,: vitis, nisi praepingui solo, non respondet,; cf.: metalla plenius responsura fodienti,.—Hence, rēspon-sum, i, n., an answer, reply, response (equally freq. in sing. and plur.).
In gen.: suis postulatis responsa exspectare,: haec paucis diebus ex illius ad nostra responsa responsis intellegentur, quorsum evasura sint,: responsum senatūs,: sine responso legatos dimisit,: nullo ab nostris dato responso,: responsum dedisti tantis de rebus,; ; so, dare responsum,; , ext. 3; ; : reddere alicui,; cf.: triste redditum,: ferre (ab aliquo),to receive,; : referre (ab aliquo),to deliver,; ; : elicere,: petere,: responsum accipere,; : responsum non fuit in eis,.—
In partic. (acc. to II. A. 2.), an answer, reply of a lawyer, priest, oracle, etc.; an opinion, response, oracle: cum responsumque ab eo (Crasso) verum magis, quam ad suam rem accommodatum abstulisset, etc.,: res judicatae, decreta, responsa,; .— The responsa prudentium, or authoritative opinions of leading lawyers, were an important source of the Roman law, Sandars ad loc.: haruspicum responsa,; cf. ; ; : legatus a Delphis Romam rediit, responsumque ex scripto recitavit,; cf. ; ; ; ; ; ; ; et saep.— In eccl. Lat.: responsum Dei, ab angelo, etc.,; ; .

la:verb:responso.html:
rēsponso, āre, v. freq. a.
id.
,
to return an answer, to answer, reply, respond (poet.).
Lit.: neu quisquam responset, quando hasce aedes pultabit senex,: pro me responsa tibi,; : num ancillae aut servi tibi Responsant?answer you back,.—
Trop.: exoritur clamor, ripaeque lacusque Responsant circa,re-echo,; ; ; : ne gallina malum responset dura palato,ill suit his palate,: responsare cupidinibus, contemnere honores Fortis,to withstand, resist, bid defiance to,; cf.: fortunae superbae,: animus cenis opimis,.

senses: to answer in writing a petition or legal question; to give a rescript or a judicial decision
to make an entry per contra; to place to one's credit; hence, to pay back, repay
to enlist under a different name, office, etc.: to transfer from one kind of troops to another
la:verb:rescribo.html:
rē-scrībo, psi, ptum, 3, v. a.
To write back or in return, to reply in writing (freq. and class.).
In gen.: antemeridianis tuis litteris heri statim rescripsi: nunc respondeo vespertinis,; so, cui rei,; 13, 21, 1; cf.: litterae mihi redditae sunt a Pompeio . . . ei statim rescripsi, non me quaerere, etc.,: ad eam (epistulam) rescribam igitur,: ad litteras,: ad ea, quae requisieras,; cf.: tibi ad ea quae quaeris,: ad Trebatium,: Pompeius rescripserat, sese, etc.,: tibi meam (epistulam), quam ad eum rescripseram, misi,: debes hoc etiam rescribere,: rescribere veteribus orationibus, to write against, reply to, ἀντιγράφειν, ; so, orationibus,: oratorum actionibus,: cujus libris de Orthographiā,; cf.: rescripta Bruto de Catone,: nil mihi rescribas,: non rescribendi gloria visa levis,: orationem, (in , descriptos is the true read.).—
In partic.
Polit. and jurid. t. t., of emperors or lawyers, to answer in writing a petition or legal question; to give a rescript or a judicial decision: Tiberio pro cliente Graeco petenti rescripsit (Augustus), non aliter se daturum quam si, etc.,; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; — Hence, rēscriptum, i, n., subst., an imperial rescript, (9): quaesitum est, an adversus rescriptum principis provocari possit,: quod et Herennio Modestino studioso meo de Dalmatiā consulenti rescripsi,; ; —
In account-books, to make an entry per contra; to place to one's credit; hence, i. q. to pay back, repay: illud mihi Argentum rursum jube rescribi,; : qui de residuis CCCC. HS. CC. praesentia solverimus, reliqua rescribamus,will place to his credit, will pay hereafter,: dictantis, quod tu numquam rescribere possis,: Darios,.—
To write over again, write anew (not anteAug.): Pollio Asinius parum diligenter compositos putat (Caesaris commentarios), existimatque rescripturum et correcturum fuisse, i. e. to revise (syn. retractare), : actiones,; cf. ; 8, 21, 6.—
In partic., in milit. lang., to enroll anew, to re-enlist: rescriptae ex eodem milite novae legiones,.—
In milit. lang., to transfer from one kind of troops to another: Caesarem decimam legionem ad equum rescribere,

la:verb:respuo.html:
rē-spŭo, ŭi, 3, v. a.,
to spit back or out; to discharge by spitting; to cast out, cast off, eject, expel, etc. (class.; esp. freq. in the trop. signif.).
Lit.: quin etiam gustatus, quam cito id, quod valde dulce est, aspernatur ac respuit,: quas natura respuerit,: lumen per cornum transit, at imber respuitur,; cf. : liquorem ab se,; cf.: ferrum ab se (opp. resorbere),; ; cf. ; : frenos cum sanguine (equus),: invisum cadaver (humus),: oleas albas propter amaritudinem respuit palatum,: respuit aqua limum,: tantum interest repercussum illum (aëra) respuat an excipiat,: respuens securis materia,; cf.: tela omnia,.—
Trop., to reject, repel, refuse; to dislike, disapprove, not accept (syn.: reprobo, reicio, repudio): quae nisi respuis ex animo longeque remittis,: cum id dicat, quod omnium mentes aspernentur ac respuant,; cf. : ratio juris respuat hanc defensionem et pro nihilo putet,; : haec aetas omne quod fieri non potest respuit,: quos et praesens et postera respuit aetas,: orationem,: quo judex dicto moveatur quid respuat,: non respuit Caesar condicionem,: Caesaris interdicta respuuntur,are spurned,; cf. : quod respuunt (aures) immutandum est,; ; ; cf.: nemo civis est, qui vos non oculis fugiat, auribus respuat, animo aspernetur,: sunt enim qui respuant (consolationem), sed refert quo modo adhibeatur,.—Absol.: quis te tum audiret illorum? respuerent aures,; ; cf.: calcitrat, respuit,.— *
Part. pres. with gen.: communium vocum respuens nimis ac fastidiens,.

la:verb:resto.gloss: to stand firm; to stay behind
senses: to stand firm; to stay behind
to remain available, to be left over
la:verb:resto.html:
rē-sto, stĭti, 1 (
perf. subj. restaverit, ), v. n.
To stop behind, keep back, stand still (very rare and only poet., whereas resisto is class.).
Lit.: si resto, pergit, ut eam: si ire conor, prohibet betere, Pac. ap. . —
Trop.: impetus haut longe mediis regionibus restat, Enn. ap. Müll. (Ann. v. 475 Vahl.): nullo dominae teritur molimine amator Restat et immerita sustinet aure minas,stands firm, holds out, (3, 20), 18. —
To withstand, resist, oppose (so less freq. than resisto, and not in Cic. or Cæs.).
Of military resistance, to stand firm, hold out, not yield; constr. usually absol.; rarely with dat. or adversum: Illyrii restant sicis sibinisque fodantes, Enn. ap. Paul. ex Müll. (Ann. v. 496 Vahl.): validam urbem multos dies restantem pugnando vicit, Sall. ap. ( Dietsch): quia summā vi restare (milites) nunciabantur, Drak.: solā virtute militum restantes caeduntur caeduntque,; ; ; 23, 45; 26, 3; 29, 2; 34, 14: dum restat Hector,: nunc in restantes mucronem comminus urget,.—Impers. pass.: ut quā minimā vi restatur, eā parte irrumpat,. — With dat.: paucis plures vix restatis,: restando adversis,.—With adversum: paulum morae attulere ferrati restantibus laminis adversum pila et gladios,.—
Apart from milit. lang., in gen.: nunc ratio nulla est restandi, nulla facultas, etc.,: is mihi, dum resto, juvenili guttura pugno Rupit,; : in quā re nunc tam confidenter restas, stulta?oppose me,; cf. . —Of things: aera claustris restantia vociferantur,: restantia claustra,.—
To be left, remain (syn. remaneo; the predominant signif. of the word; most freq. in the third person): hujus generis reliquias Restare video,: ego conviviis delector nec cum aequalibus solum qui pauci jam admodum restant, sed cum vestrā etiam aetate,: ego vivendo vici mea fata, superstes Restarem ut genitor,: de bonis quod restat reliquiarum,; cf. : unam sibi spem reliquam in Etruscis restare,; Orell.: quae (studia) sola ei in malis restiterunt,: omnes composui. Felices! Nunc ego resto,; : de viginti Restabam solus,: jam labor exiguus Phoebo restabat,: duae restant noctes de mense secundo,: si e nobis aliquid nisi umbra restat,: jam duo restabant fata tum,: qui e divisione tripartitā duas partes absolverit, huic necesse est restare tertiam,: infinitae caedi,: dona ferens pelago et flammis restantia Trojae, left, remaining from the sea, etc., : unum etiam restat amico nostro ad omne dedecus, ut, etc.,: hoc unum restabat, ut,; cf.: illud etiam restiterat, ut, etc.,.— Impers.: restat, ut aut summa neglegentia tibi obstiterit, aut, etc.,; so, restat, ut,; init.; —With inf. (mostly poet.): nec aliud restabat quam corrigere, etc.,: restabat aliud nihil, nisi oculos pascere,; ; .—
In partic., with reference to the future, to remain for, await one (rare and mostly poet.): quid restat, nisi porro ut fiam miser,: placet (vobis) socios sic tractari, quod restat, ut per haec tempora tractatos videtis?i. e. hereafter, for the future,: nudus humi jacet infans ... ut aequom est, cui tantum in vitā restet transire malorum,; : hoc Latio restare canunt,; .

la:verb:restinguo.gloss: to put out, quench or extinguish
senses: to put out, quench or extinguish
la:verb:restinguo.html:
rē-stinguo, nxi, nctum, 3, v. a.,
to put out, quench, extinguish (class.).
Lit.: ignem restinguunt aquā,; so, ignem, (with refrigerare); ; ; ; , praef. 1, § 1; : flammam,; ; : incendium, Catil. ap. ; id ap. ; : restincto aggere,; : aes accensum,: lucernam,: fulminis ictum,: solem,: favillas ardentes lacte,: faces,.— Absol.: ut omnis ex castris multitudo ad restinguendum concurreret,to extinguish the flames,: aquam ad restinguendum ferre,; cf.: omnes restinguere velle videres,.—
Transf., to quench, slake, assuage, allay, mitigate, counteract, etc.: sitim,; : pocula ardentis Falerni lymphā,: venena,; ; : ictus scorpionis, et saep.—
Trop., to extinguish, exterminate, annihilate, destroy: tum igitur tibi aquae erit cupido, genus qui restinguas tuom,: haustas sanguisugas,i. e. to kill,: pilos spumā inlitā,,

§ 252: morbum,; cf. nauseam,: haec verba una mehercle falsa lacrimula Restinguet,: illam Ut ne restinguas lacrimis,: animos hominum sensusque morte restingui,: mentes inflammatas,; cf.: bellum restinctum (opp. inflammatum),: oriens incendium belli sanguine suo,: omnium cupiditatum ardorem,; cf.: illā tertiā parte animi, in quā irarum exsistit ardor, sedatā atque restinctā,appeased,: cupiditates iracundiasque (eloquentiā), Orell. N. cr.: odium,: studia,; : animorum incendia,: sermunculum omnem aut restinxerit aut sedarit,: ardentem Italiam,: rabies restinguitur,.

la:noun:restitutio.html:
rēstĭtūtĭo, ōnis, f.
restituo
,
a restoring, restoration.
In gen.: domus incendio absumptae,i. e. a rebuilding,: Capitolii,: theatri,: urbis in majus,: afflictarum civitatum,.—Trop.: omnis pristinae fortunae,: libertatis,, ext. 4: lunae,. —
In partic.
A giving back, restitution (in jurid. Lat.), ; ; .—
The act of replacing, reinstating one condemned or proscribed in his former condition; the restoration of rights which have been forfeited by law: damnatorum,; : salus restitutioque,a recalling from exile,; ; : in integrum restitutiones, (v. this entire section: De in integrum restitutionibus); 4, 4, 18, § 1; 4, 4, 20 pr.

senses: to remain behind, be left behind
la:verb:resideo.html:
rĕ-sĭdĕo, sēdi, 2, v. n. and a.
[sedeo], to sit back, remain sitting anywhere (cf. resisto); to remain behind, to remain, rest, linger, tarry, abide, reside (syn. remaneo; class.).
Lit.: sine mente animoque nequit residere per artus pars ulla animai,: piger pandi tergo residebat aselli,: in tergo,; cf.: Acidis in gremio (latitans),resting,: in hoc facto de cautibus antro,residing,; cf.: Erycina Monte suo residens,: in villā,: si te interfici jussero, residebit in re publicā reliqua conjuratorum manus,: corvus altā arbore residens, (but the correct read., , is residamus; v. Madv. ad h. l.).— In perf.: Lydum patriis in terris resedisse, Tyrrheno datum novas ut conderet sedes,: in oppido aliquo mallem resedisse, quoad arcesserer,: erravitne viā seu lassa resedit, Incertum,remained behind,; cf.: fessus valle,: lassus in humo,: medio rex ipse resedit Agmine,: orba resedit Exanimes inter natos natasque,: saxo resedit Pastor,. — Act. (very rare): dorsum meum residebat,. —
To sit up, assume a sitting posture (late Lat.): et resedit qui erat mortuus,. —
Meton., to sit inactive, to remain idle or listless (rare): artifex cum exprimere vellet Athamantis furorem Learcho filio praecipitato residentis poenitentiā,sitting listlessly subdued by remorse,: miles residet,. — Hence, act., to keep or celebrate a holiday: venter gutturque resident esuriales ferias (v. esurialis),. — Pass.: nec vero tam denicales (quae a nece appellatae sunt, quia residentur mortuis) quam ceterorum caelestium quieti dies Feriae nominarentur,because they are kept in honor of the dead, Creuz (codd. leg. residentur mortui; B. and K. resident mortui; cf.I.supra).—
Trop., to remain behind, remain, be left (a favorite word with Cic.; syn.: resto, supersum); constr most freq., in aliquā re: in corpore perspicuum est, vel exstincto animo vel elapso, nullum residere sensum,; cf. : si ex tanto latrocinio iste unus tolletur, periculum residebit,: ne quas inimicitias residere in familiis nostris arbitretur,, B, § 4; cf.: in vobis resident mores pristini,: qui ullas resedisse in te simultatis reliquias senserit,: si quid amoris erga me in te residet,: etiam nunc residet spes in virtute tuā,: quorum non in sententiā solum, sed etiam in nutu residebat auctoritas,: quorum in consilio pristinae residere virtutis memoria videtur,.—With dat.: cum horum tectis et sedibus residere aliquod bellum semper videtur,.— With apud: apud me plus officii residere facile patior,: hujus incommodi culpa ubi resideat, facilius possum existimare quam scribere,: si qua (ira) ex certamine residet,. — Business t. t., to be or remain behind, i. e. to be unaccounted for, in default: pecunia publica resedit apud aliquem,.

la:verb:resido.gloss: to sit, to settle in a place
senses: to sit, to settle in a place
la:verb:resido.html:
rĕ-sīdo, sēdi (in some MSS. also rĕsīdi), 3, v. n.,
to sit down, to settle anywhere (class.).
Lit.: residamus, si placet, Madv. N. cr.: in ripă inambulantes, tum vero residentes,: (aves) plurimum volant ... cetera genera residunt et insistunt,: mediis residunt Aedibus,: Siculis arvis,: residunt In partem, quae peste caret,: loci amoenitate captos in iisdem terris cum virgine resedisse, . — Poet.: jam jam residunt cruribus asperae Pelles,settle, gather,. — In perf.: consessu exstructo resedit,. —
Transf., of things, to settle or sink down, to sink, subside (cf. consido and decido): si montes resedissent,: (Nilus) residit iisdem quibus accrevit modis (opp. crescit),; ; cf.: maria in se ipsa residant (opp. tumescant),; : residentibus flammis,.—
Trop. (acc. to I. B.), to sink or settle down, to abate, grow calm, subside: cum venti posuere omnisque repente resedit Flatus,: sex mihi surgat opus numeris (i. e. in the hexameter), m quinque residat (i. e. in the pentameter), (cf. Coleridge's "falling in melody back"): (poëma) apte et varie nunc attollebatur, nunc residebat,: si contrarius ventus resedisset,: cum tumor animi resedisset,; cf.: Marcelli impetus, Cael. ap. : impetus animorum ardorque,: ardor,; cf.: sed propera ne vela cadant auraeque residant,: irae,: terror,: bellum,; : clandestinis nunciis Allobrogas sollicitat, quorum mentes nondum ab superiore bello resedisse sperabat,: longiore certamine sensim residere Samnitium animos,: ardorem eum, qui resederat, excitare rursus,: tumida ex ira corda,.

la:adj:residuus.html:
rĕsĭdŭus, a, um, adj.
resideo
,
that is left behind, that remains over and above, remaining, residuary; subst., the remainder, residue, rest (class.; cf.: reliquus, superstes): odium,: sollicitudo, Planc. ap. : ex residuā vetere simultate,; cf. : irae bellorum,; cf. bellum,: nomen libertatis (with reliqua umbra),: residuae integraeque etiam nunc (copiae),; cf.: manus Spartaci et Catilinae,; and: stirps horum,: quid potest esse in calamitate residui, quod, etc.,; cf.: ne cui residui spiritus quicquam inesset,: residui nobilium,: paucos comites residuos fortuna fecit,; : residuum cibariorum,; cf.: nihil residuum crudelitatis,: residua diurni actūs conficere,.—
In business lang., of a payment, outstanding, due: pecuniae,; ; so, summae,: quid relatum, quid residuum sit,.— Plur. subst.: rĕsĭdŭae, ārum, f. (sc. pecuniae), arrears, dues: vectigalium,: lege Juliā de residuis tenetur, qui publicam pecuniam delegatam in usum aliquem retinuit neque in eum consumpsit,; cf. and 16.?*! In the fragment of Attius ap. Müll. (Trag. Rel. p. 192 Rib.), perh. = reses, slothfui, inactive; cf.: residuus quasi tardus, Placid. Gloss.

la:verb:reservo.gloss: to reserve, retain, save; to keep or hold back or in reserve
senses: to reserve, retain, save; to keep or hold back or in reserve
la:verb:reservo.html:
rĕ-servo, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.,
to keep back, save up, qs. for future use; to reserve (very freq. and class.; cf. repono); constr.: aliquid (aliquem) ad aliquid, in aliquid, alicui, with a terminal adv. or absol.
With ad: reliquas merces commeatusque ad obsidionem urbis,: philosophorum libros sibi ad Tusculani requiem atque otium,; : aliquid ad testes,: vitam suam ad incertissimam spem,: hoc consilium ad extremum,: ad ejus periculum legiones,: consulem non ad vitam suam sed ad salutem vestram,: te ad aliquod severius judicium, id. Or. in Tog. Cand. (tom. ii. 1, p. 523 Orell.): vos ad eam rem,: testem ad extremum,: nonne et hominem ipsum ad dubia rei publicae tempora reservandum?(15, 32): utinam ad illa tempora me fortuna reservavisset!: se ad majora,.—
With in: inimicitiasque in aliud tempus reservare,: poenas praesentis fraudis in diem,: partem (stercoris) in pratum,: aliquem in aliud tempus,; : aliquos in unum pugnae laborem,.—
With dat.: natura reservans semina rebus,: illorum esse praedam atque illis reservari,: causam a judicibus praetermissam ipsis (decemviris),: scientiam rei mihi,: tibi se peritura Pergama,: cetera praesenti sermoni,; : ista judicia melioribus meis rebus,: se temporibus aliis,: me Minucio et Salvio,: nos reipublicae,: te non urbi sed carceri,: cui te exitio,: incolumem Pallanta mihi si fata reservant,: se judiciis posterorum,: supplicia alicui,.— *
With a terminal adv.: quid hoc homine facias? aut quo civem importunum reserves?.—(ε) With a simple object, to keep from perishing, to save, preserve (very rare): vide ne, cum velis revocare tempus omnium reservandorum, cum qui servetur non erit, non possis, Orell. N. cr.; cf.: partum reservare,: reservatis Haeduis atque Arvernis,: hominem,: gladiatores,: quaesitique tenax et qui quaesita reservent,.

la:verb:respicio.gloss: to look behind, look back at or upon, look to, look around

to have a care for, regard, be mindful of, consider, respect
la:verb:respicio.html:
rē-spĭcĭo, spexi, spectum, 3 (old form of
subj. perf. respexis, ; ; ), v. n. and a., to look back or behind, to look about, look; to see behind one; to look back upon, to look at, look to or for any thing (very freq. and class.).
Lit.
Neutr.: respicere quasi retro aspicere, Varro Manio: sedens ... neque post respiciens, neque ante prospiciens, (cf. infra, β): longe retro respicere non possunt,; ; cf. : subito exaudivit hinnitum respexitque et equum alacrem laetus aspexit,fin.: Er. Ergasilum qui vocat? He. Respice ... respice ad me, : huc ad aliquem,; so, ad aliquem,; ; ; ; ; ; ; cf.: nocte ad oppidum,: patriae ad oras,: ad libellos,; ; : ad laevam,: in aliquem,: huc,; ; ; : tanta militum virtus fuit, ut non modo de vallo decederet nemo, sed paene ne respiceret quidem quisquam,: transque caput jace, nec respexeris,: respicit Aeneas subito,: a tergo,: quod respicere vetitus est,.—
Act. (in lit. sense rare in good prose, but freq. in all styles in the trop. signif.; v.infra, II.): ipsi Respiciunt atram in nimbo volitare favillam,look back on, see behind them,: modo Prospicit occasus, interdum respicit ortus,: respice me et relinque egentem parasitum,: repudia istos comites atque hoc respice et revortere,: proxima respiciens signa,; cf. Caesarem,: (Hannibalem) respexisse saepe Italiae litora,: nec prius amissam (Creüsam) respexi animumve reflexi, Quam, etc.,. 741; ; ; cf.: ut stetit et frustra absentem respexit amicum,: instantem tergo Cloanthum,: donec versas ad litora puppes Respiciunt,; cf. : oculis pignora cara,: medio cum Sol altissimus orbe Tantum respiceret, quantum superesse videret, looked back upon, i. e. had already passed over, . —
Trop.
In gen., to look, have regard, turn attention.
Neutr.: neque se in multa simul intendere animus totum potest: et, quocumque respexit, desinit intueri, quod propositum erat,at whatsoever it looks,: si propter singula verba ad singulas formas respiciendum erit,; cf.: non respiciendum ad haec,: M. Bibulus cuncta administrabat: ad hunc summa imperii respiciebat,looked to him, was centred in him,; cf.: periculum (emptionis) ad venditorem respicere, (with ad venditorem pertinere). —
Act., to look at, regard, look to: quom respicias immensi temporis omne Praeteritum spatium,; cf.: quoad longissime potest mens mea respicere spatium praeteriti temporis,: cum vastitatem Italiae respexerint, Asin. Poll. ap. : subsidia, quae respicerent in re trepidā, etc., which they might look to, i. e. from which they might expect aid, ; cf.: ne respicere spem ullam ab Romanis posset,: respicere exemplar vitae morumque jubebo Doctum imitatorem,to look at, have in his eye,: de te pendentis, te respicientis amici,. — With rel.-clause: quid sit prius actum, respicere aetas Nostra nequit, nisi, etc.,; cf. : respiciens, an vera soror,.—
Pregn., to look at with solicitude, i. e. to have a care for, regard, be mindful of, consider, respect, etc. (in this sense mostly act.; cf. provideo).
Of a protecting deity: di homines respiciunt,: deus respiciet nos aliquis,; ; : nisi quis nos deus respexerit,:

Sive neglectum genus et nepotes Respicis auctor, ; : nisi idem deus, qui, etc., respexerit rem publicam,: et me et te, nisi quid dī respiciunt, perdidi,.— Hence, Rēspĭcĭens, the Provident, an epithet of Fortuna: ad opem ferendam,; ; .— Rarely, in a bad sense, of an avenging deity: at vos, devota capita, respiciant di perjuriorum vindices,may they remember it against you,.—

Of persons that have a care or regard for any thing: hercle alius nemo respicit nos,; so, aliquem,; : age, me in tuis secundis respice,; : miseros aratores,; : sin Caesarem respiciant,; : non Pylium Nestora respicis,: quantum quisque ferat respiciendus erit,: mox deos respexere; restitui Capitolium placuit,bethought themselves of,: aetatem tuam,: populi Romani commoda (with prospicere),: salutem cum meam tum aliorum,; cf. : rem publicam,; Planc. ap. : mala sua, et saep. —With se, to think of or have regard for one's self, ; ; ; ; id. pro Scaur. Fragm. 41, p. 267 Orell.: quod si Caesar se respexerit, Planc. ap. .—With ad (Quintilian): ad utilitatem Ligarii respicit,looks to the advantage of,; so, modice ad hanc partem,: Graecas litteras (corresp. to studere Latinis),: saepius ad curam rerum ab elocutione,.—With an abstr. subj.: si quid pietas antiqua labores Respicit humanos,.— With object-clause, to observe, perceive, notice: respicio nihili meam vos gratiam facere,.

la:verb:resono.gloss: to sound or ring again, resound, reecho; call repeatedly
senses: to sound or ring again, resound, reecho; call repeatedly
to give back the sound of, resound, reecho with
la:verb:resono.html:
rĕ-sŏno, āvi, 1 (ante-class. collat. form, acc. to the 3d conj., resonit, Pac. and Att. ap. : resonunt, Enn. and Att. ap. P.; of the
perf. only resonavit, ), v. n. and a., to sound or ring again, to resound, re-echo (freq. and class.).
Neutr.
Lit.: tum clupei resonunt, Enn. l. l. (Ann. v. 364 Vahl.): valvae resonunt regiae, Att. l. l.: theatrum naturā ita resonans, ut, etc.,: venenum sic e poculo ejecit, ut id resonaret,: ubi non resonent imagines,i. e. where no echoes are heard, without echoes,: cum frustra resonant aera,: resonabat eburnea Telorum custos

(i. e. pharetra), : ut solent pleni resonare camini,to send forth a roaring noise,: eque sacrā resonant examina quercu,: hominum clamor et tubarum sonus amplior quam editur resonare solet,: resonantia litora,. — With abl.: clamore et gemitu templum resonit caelitum, Att. ap. Non. l. l.: aura crepitu musico, Pac. l. l.: late plangoribus aedes,: domus undique magno strepitu,: latratibus aether,: spectacula plausu,: avibus virgulta canoris,: arbusta cicadis,. — Poet., with acc.: litoraque alcyonen resonant, acalanthida dumi,resound with,: testudo septem nervis,; cf.: vox ima quattuor chordis,. — With ad: qui (cornus) ad nervos resonant in cantibus,. — With dat.: suave locus voci resonat conclusus,echoes to the voice,; cf.: carmina resonantia chordis Romanis, to the strings, Auct. Pan. ad Pis. 229. —

Trop., to resound, re-echo: in vocibus nostrorum oratorum recinit quiddam et resonat urbanius,; cf. .—With dat.: gloria virtuti resonat tamquam imago,. —
Act., to give back the sound of, to resound, re-echo with any thing: formosam resonare doces Amaryllida silvas,; so, triste et acutum,: resonent mihi Cynthia silvae,call out to me, Cynthia,: ora Hylan semper resonantia,; cf. . — Pass.: (sonus) in fidibus testudine resonatur aut cornu,. — Poet., with acc. of a place, to make resound or re-echo: ubi Solis filia lucos Assiduo resonat cantu,. —
To say urgently or continually (late Lat.): vernacula principi,.

la:verb:resurgo.html:
rĕ-surgo, surrexi, surrectum, 3, v. n.,
to rise or raise one's self again, to appear again (poet. and post-Aug.; once in Liv. with velut; v.infra).
Lit.: pugnat resurgere saepe,: si resurgat centimanus Gyges,; ; cf., of convalescent persons: resurgam,.— Esp., to rise again, rise from the grave (eccl. Lat.): ab inferis,; ; ; .—Of things: cupressus arbor repente prociderat ac postero die eodem vestigio resurgens procera et latior virebat,; ; : herbae,: obruta cymba de mediis aquis,: orbe lunaria cornua nono,; ; : urbs,is rebuilt,.—
Trop. (cf. resisto): cum res Romana velut resurgeret,; cf.: illic fas regna resurgere Trojae,; and with this cf.: arma resurgentis Trojae (i.e. Romae),87 (53 M.): victa tamen vinces, eversaque Troja, resurges,: resurgens Saevit amor,: bellum,; : rabies,: partes in Africā,: legiones resurgere in ultionem properent,: cum eum ceteri ita vicerint ut major instaurando bello resurgeret,: ac ne tam longā quidem aetate, quae excidium ejus secuta est, resurrexit,: resurgit verae virtutis fortior fama,: ter si resurgat murus aëneus,.

la:adj:resupinus.html:
rĕ-sŭpīnus, a, um, adj.,
bent back or backwards, lying on one's back or with the face upwards, supine (not in Cic.).
Lit.: resupinum in caelo contueri, i. e. lying on

one's back, face upwards, supine, Att. ap. : fertur equis curruque haeret resupinus inani,: eque tuo pendet resupino spiritus ore,; ; : jacuit resupinus humi,; 12, 324: hunc ego resupinum fudi, al.: retro lentas tendo resupinus habenas,bent back,: collum,: pectus,: caput, et saep. — Of an arrogant gait or manner: (Niobe) mediam tulerat gressus resupina per urbem, with head thrown back, i. e. proudly, ; cf. ; Cod. Th. 9, 3, 6: si non resupini spectantesque tectum expectaverimus, quid obveniat,: spectat resupino sidera vultu,.—

Transf., of things turned or bent back: Elis,spread out on a hill,: labra lilii,: vomer,.—
Trop., lazy, slothful, effeminate, careless, negligent: voluptas,; cf. : qui solvit, numquam ita resupinus est, ut facile suas pecunias jactet,: existimatio,.

la:verb:respecto.gloss: to look back, around, continuously or intently
senses: to look back, around, continuously or intently
la:verb:respecto.html:
respecto, āre,
v. freq. n. and a. [id.], to look back, look round or behind repeatedly or intently, to look or gaze about; to look at any thing (class.).
Lit.
Neutr. absol.: quid respectas? nihil pericli est,: ubi respectantes hostium antesignanos vidit,; ; : respectans abit,; : ad tribunal,: respecto identidem, ne senex, etc.,; so, identidem, ne,. — Poet.: leti janua patet immani et vasto respectat hiatu,.—
Act.: dictatore arcem Romanam respectante,: funera respectans,: sine fine Caesarem,: alium (alius),: suos,.—
Trop., to cast a look behind, to wait; to wait for, look for, expect; to care for, regard, respect.
Neutr.: verum haec ita praetereamus, ut tamen intuentes et respectantes relinquamus,: animus non me deserens, sed respectans in ea loca discessit, id. : taciti respectabant somnoque sepulti, Dum, etc.,i. e. waited,. —
Act.: si qua pios respectant numina,regard,: neque hoc liberis nostris interdicendum est, ne observent tribules suos ... ne par ab iis munus in suā petitione respectent,look for, expect,: meum amorem,.

la:verb:resolvo.gloss: to release, loosen, unloose, unbind, disentangle, relax, dissolve
senses: to release, loosen, unloose, unbind, disentangle, relax, dissolve
la:verb:resolvo.html:
rĕ-solvo, solvi, sŏlūtum, 3, v. a.,
to untie, unfasten, unbind; to loose, loosen, release, open (not freq. till after the Aug. per.; cf.: relaxo, resero, recludo, libero).
Lit.
In gen.: equos,to unyoke,; cf.: juncta juga leonibus,: quem suā sponte vinxerit, non resolvat, etc.,; : cinctas vestes,; cf. nodum,: fila,to loose, separate,: vulnera,to unbind,; : oras,to cast loose from the shore, Drak. N. cr.: virginem catenis,i. e. to release,; cf.: crura vinclis,: (puella) resoluta capillos,: claustra,to open,: litteras,: venas,: jugulum mucrone,: ferro,: manum in diversum,: fauces haec in verba,; cf.: exspectato Ora sono,, 126: fatis ora,; and simply ora,: ignis aurum resolvit,melts, dissolves,: nivem,to melt, thaw,; cf.: resolutus repente Rhenus,: margaritas in tabem,: glaebam in pulverem,: nummos,to melt down, — Poet.: nebulas ventis ac sole,to disperse, dissipate, scatter,; cf. tenebras (sidere),: resoluta caligo,: Zephyro se glaeba, becomes loose or soft, ; : terra resoluta,; : muros ariete,to break down,: cinctos muros,: saxa,. —
In partic.
To relax, unnerve, enervate, enfeeble the body (cf. remitto): felicitas hos inflat, illos mollit et totos resolvit,: (Cerberus) immania terga resolvit Fusus humi,stretched out,: nexos artus,: utrumque (concubitus),: corpus (somno),: placitā resoluta quiete,: membra ad molles choros, (3, 32), 42; : fatigatione resolutus,; .—
Mostly ante-class., to pay a debt: minas,: argentum,; : pro vecturā,; cf. ; ; : damnum boni viri arbitratu resolvere,. —
Trop.
In gen. (acc. to I. A.), to separate, unbind, set free, release; to disclose, show, reveal, lay open; to annul, cancel, make void, abolish, destroy (syn. rescindo): ipsas periodos majoribus intervallis et velut laxioribus nodis resolvemus,: quoniam, quā fieri quicquid posset ratione, resolvi,have disclosed, shown,: teque piacula nulla resolvent,release,: amore resolutus,: (Hannibal) Quod sponte abscedat tandemque resolvat Ausoniam,liberate,: resoluta legibus urbs,: ira resoluta frenis legum,: litem quod lite resolvit,does away with, ends,: invitat genialis hiems curasque resolvit,banishes, dispels,: tristitiam animi,: dolos tecti ambagesque,i. e. find the way through,: jura (pudoris),: dolos fraudesque,: gaudia ferro,: amphiboliam,to destroy, remove,: ambiguitatem,: dicta ex parte diversā,i. e. refute,: vectigal et onera commerciorum,to abolish,: stipulationem,: conventionem,: emptionem, et saep. —
In partic. (acc. to I. B.).
To relax, soften: disciplinam militarem,: judices,; —
To pay: unā plagā (cf. I. B. 2. supra), (but in , the correct reading is persoluturum). — Hence, rĕsŏlūtus, a, um, P. a. (acc. to I. B. 1.), relaxed, enervated, effeminate: corpora juvenum (with fluxa), Col. praef. § 17: minister Idaeo resolutior cinaedo,.—
Free, unhampered: os, Val.Max. 8, 7, ext. 1.—
Unbridled: gaudia,.—Adv.: rĕsŏlūtē, without restraint: quo resolutius decachinnetis,more unrestrainedly,.

la:verb:resigno.html:
rĕ-signo, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
To unseal, open (class.).
Lit.: litteras,; : testamenta,; ; : loculos,.—Poet.: perjuria Graia resignat,breaks through the faithless band,: (Mercurius) lumina morte resignat, opens the eyes of the dead whom he is about to conduct to Orcus, .—
Trop.
To annul, cancel, invalidate, rescind, destroy (syn.: rescindere, dissolvere): tabularum fidem,: ne quid ex constituti fide resignaret,violate, Duker: pacta,: jura leti (Mercurius),: quorum mors resignata est,—
To disclose, reveal (only poet.): venientia fata,: hoc, quod latet, etc.,: verba, . —
Ante-class. and in Hor. = rescribere (I. B. 2.), to transfer in an account; to assign to one: resignare antiqui dicebant pro rescribere, ut adhuc subsignare dicimus pro subscribere, Müll.: resignatum aes dicitur militi, cum ob delictum aliquod jussu tribuni militum, ne stipendium ei detur, in tabulas refertur. Signare enim dicebant pro scribere, id. pp. 284 and 285 ib.; Cato ap. . — Hence, to give back, resign, = reddere: laudo manentem (Fortunam): si celeres quatit Pennas, resigno quae dedit,: cuncta resigno,.

senses: to follow as a consequence, to come up logically
la:verb:resulto.html:
rĕsulto, no
perf., ātum, 1, v. freq. n. and a. [resilio], to spring or leap back, to rebound (poet. and in post-Aug. prose; only of inanimate or abstract subjects).
Lit.: (corpora) conflicta resultant, etc., and 101: tela irrita galeā clipeoque,: aqua objectu lapillorum,; cf.: unda scissa, Petr. poët. Sat. 89, 2, 31: illisum caput scopulis resultat,.— Of animals: resultabunt canes ululantibus lupis, Amm 31, 1, 2.—
In partic., of sound, to reverberate, resound, re-echo: ubi concava pulsu Saxa sonant vocisque offensa resultat imago,: inimica est (apibus) echo resultanti sono,: murmur in duris,. —
Transf., of places or things that return a sound, to resound, re-echo, reverberate, ring, etc.: pulsati colles clamore resultant,: colles,: saltus,: juga longa,: tecta vocibus,: aera percussis incudibus,: parma pulsu umbonum,: resultantibus armis et tubis,: resultantibus lituis,.—With a homogeneous object: sonum (saxa),; .—
Trop., of pronunciation, etc., to leap, hop: (verba) ne brevium (syllabarum) contexu resultent, produce a jumping or jerking effect, : praeceps ac resultans (in oratione, opp. tardum et segne),; cf. ; : ut barbara nomina Graecis versibus non resultent,i. e. are unfit for, unsuiled to,.

la:verb:respergo.html:
rē-spergo, si, sum, 3, v. a.,
to sprinkle over any thing; to besprinkle, bestrew (rare but class.).
Lit.: praetoris oculos,: manus, os, simulacrum sanguine,: morientium sanguine os uxoris respersum,; ; cf.: aliquem cruore,: sanguine dextram,; : comae respersae sanguine,: caede fraternā juvenis respersus, Cat 64, 181; ; : se sanguine nefando,: quidquid fuerat mortale aquis,: vino rogum ne respargito, Lex Numae ap. ; cf. Müll.: alicubi labi necesse est, alicubi respergi,to be splashed, spattered,: pelagus respergit, Att. ap. . — Poet.: cum primum Aurora respergit lumine terras, Lucr. ap. (cf. spargit, ): nullā nube respersus jubar,i. e. beclouded, dimmed,. — *
Transf., to spread out: ut nux repercussa radicem respergat,. —
Trop., to besprinkle, bespatter, defile, etc.: servili probro respersus est,: aliquem infamiā,.

la:verb:resero.html:
rĕ-sĕro, sēvi, 3, v. a.,
to sow or plant again; to plant with any thing, Müll.; ; ; .

la:verb:respiro.gloss: to blow or breathe back; to breathe out, exhale
senses: to blow or breathe back; to breathe out, exhale
to take breath; to breathe, respire
to fetch one's breath again, recover breath; to recover, revive, be relieved or refreshed after anything difficult
la:verb:respiro.html:
rē-spīro, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a. and n.
Lit., to blow or breathe back; to breathe out, exhale (class.; esp. in the trop. signif.): quod nisi respirent venti, vis nulla refrenet Res ... nunc quia respirant, etc.,: cum aspera arteria ad pulmones usque pertineat excipiatque animam eam, quae ducta sit spiritu eandemque a pulmonibus respiret et reddat,: ex eā pars redditur respirando,: malignum aëra,to exhale, send forth,; cf. ; and poet.: fistula,i. e. to sound,.—
Transf., in gen., to take breath; to breathe, respire (only neutr.).
Lit.: propius fore eos ad respirandum,; : sine respirem, quaeso, (with recipere anhelitum); : O Clitopho, timeo. Clit. respiro, ; ; : ut non ter deciens respiret,—
Trop., to fetch one's breath again, to recover breath; to recover, revive, be relieved or refreshed after any thing difficult (as labor, care, etc.); constr. absol. or ab aliquā re.
Absol.: (improbitas) cujus in animo versatur, numquam sinit eum respirare, numquam acquiescere,; cf.: si armis positis civitas respiraverit, (with recreari): cum tot negotiis distentus sit, ut libere respirare non possit,: respiravi, liberatus sum,: homines respirasse videbantur,; ; , a, 3; 10, 1: spatium respirandi dare,; fin.; 28, 31; : quo animi respirant,.—Impers. pass.: ita respiratum, mittique legationes coeptae,.—
With ab: respirare a metu,; : ab eorum mixtis precibus minisque, Liv 4, 25: a continuis cladibus,; cf.: aures poëticis voluptatibus a forensi asperitate,.—
Transf., twice in Cic., of the exertion or passion itself, to abate, diminish, cease (syn.: remittere, cessare): oppugnatio respiravit,: cupiditas atque avaritia respirasset,.
la:verb:respiro.inflection: āvi, ātum, 1, v. a. and n.

la:verb:resorbeo.gloss: to suck back, swallow again; suppress (of tears, etc.)
senses: to suck back, swallow again; suppress (of tears, etc.)
la:verb:resorbeo.html:
rĕ-sorbĕo, ēre, v. a.,
to suck back, swallow again (poet. and in post-Aug. prose): quaeque vomit fluctus totidem totidemque resorbet,; so, saxa (pontus), Wagn.: mare in se resorberi videbamus,: mare accrescere aut resorberi,: te rursus in bellum resorbens Unda fretis tulit aestuosis,: hamum (opp. egerunt),: (lapidis aestus) respuit ab se Atque per aes agitat, sine eo quod saepe resorbet,i. e. draws to itself, attracts,; so, spiritum,to suck in,: carptim vocem,: fletum,to suppress,; : lacrimas,.

la:verb:resplendeo.gloss: to shine (back) brightly, glitter; to be resplendent
senses: to shine (back) brightly, glitter; to be resplendent
la:verb:resplendeo.html:
rē-splendĕo, ēre, v. n.,
to shine brightly; to glitter, be resplendent (poet.): fulvā resplendent fragmina harenā,; ; ; ; : sidera,: facies,.— Trop.: resplendet gloria Martis,.

la:noun:resurrectio.html:
rĕsurrectĭo, ōnis, f.
resurgo
, in eccl. Lat.,
a rising again from the dead, resurrection, ; , 22, 28; ; ; ; : dominica (i. e. Domini),.

la:verb:resumo.html:
rĕ-sūmo, mpsi, mptum, 3, v. a.,
to take up again, take back, resume (poet. and in post-Aug. prose).
Lit. (terra) gentes omnis peperit et resumit denuo, Enn. ap. Müll. (Epich. v. 4 Vahl. p. 168): positas (tabellas) resumit,: tela,: librum perlectum utique ex integro,: librum in manus,: pugillares,: cito elapsum baculum,: fuscinam,: arma,; ; fin.: praetextas (opp. exuere),: pennas,: speciem caelestem,.—
Trop.: instat anhelanti prohibetque resumere vires, to get or receive again, to recover, ; so, vires,; ; : potentiam,: interruptum somnum,: animum,: animam,; cf.: resumpto spiritu recreatus est,: nomen gentile (opp. deponere),: sacramentum Vespasiani,: militiam,; cf. pugnam,to renew,: hostilia,: dominationem per arma,: libertatem,; ; : curas,: nomen,: instituta cultumque patrium,: voluptates (with repetere sollemnia), et saep.: aegrotantem,to restore,; ; .

la:noun:resolutio.html:
rĕsŏlūtĭo, ōnis, f.
resolvo
,
an untying, unbinding, loosening (not ante-Aug.).
Lit., a slackening, relaxing; a laxness, looseness, weakness: lori,: ventris, stomachi, nervorum, oculorum,; ; ; 3, 27, 1; 6, 6, 36.—
Trop.
A making void, a cancelling: venditionis,.—
A solution: sophismatis,an explanation, (dub.). —
A release, escape (late Lat.), .

la:noun:respectus.html:
respectus, ūs, m.
respicio
,
a looking back or about (class.).
Lit.: fugientibus miserabilem respectum incendiorum fore,: sine respiratione ac respectu pugnabant,: effuse ac sine respectu fugit,: sine respectu mea fata relinquens,. —
Meton., a refuge, retreat, asylum: ad Romanos,: respectum pulcherrimum et praesidium firmissimum adimit rei publicae,; ; ; cf.: omnium rerum respectum praeterquam victoriam nobis abscindamus,.: in idolis nationum non erit respectus,. —
Trop., respect, regard, consideration (cf. ratio; in this signif. rare before the Aug. per., and usu. in abl.; a favorite word of Liv.): respectum ad senatum et ad bonos non habere,: ad Romanos,: ni respectus equitum praepedisset animos,: Romanorum maxime respectus civitates movit,; : respectum amicitiae habere,; . — Abl.: respectu, by a regard, with regard; with gen.: factione respectuque rerum privatarum Appius vicit,by a regard for private interests,; so ; ; ; 42, 9; 45, 18; ; : respectu cupiunt hic tamen esse sui,; : in illius respectum iste populo praesideat,: sine respectu non majestatis modo sed etiam humanitatis,: sine respectu pudoris,; (7), 23, 2: sine respectu veniae,: fabulae,: paucitatis,: amicitiae,: sine respectu sui,: Graecum proverbium jactans: occultae musicae nullum esse respectum,is in no repute, (cf.: musicam quae sit abscondita, eam esse nullius rei,; Gr. τῆς λανθανούσης μουσικῆς οὐδεὶς λόγος).

la:noun:responsio.html:
rēsponsĭo, ōnis, f.
respondeo
.
An answer, reply; a refutation (rare but class.; syn. responsum): in quo erat accusatoris interpretatio indigna responsione,; : responsio mollis frangit iram,.— In plur., .—
In rhet.: sibi ipsi responsio, a replying to one's ownargument, ; ; (cf.: ut quasi ad interrogata sibi ipse respondeat,).

la:verb:restringo.gloss: to draw back tightly, bind back or fast, tighten
senses: to draw back tightly, bind back or fast, tighten
la:verb:restringo.html:
rēstringo, inxi, ictum, 3, v. a.
To draw back tightly; to bind back, bind fast, tighten, etc. (in the verb. finit. not anteAug., but in the P. a. class.; syn. religo).
Lit.: laevam,: restrictis ad terga manibus,: manus,: lacertos,; cf.: restringitur vinculis,; and: si manus manicis restringantur,; cf. also: Prometheus quondam silici restrictus membra catenā,: vinclo fasciae in modum laquei restricto,.—
Trop., to restrain, confine, restrict, check, etc. (syn. retineo): homines ad custodiam pecuniae,: liberalitatem,: sumptus candidatorum ambitūs lege,: delicias frugalitate,fin.: animum maestitiā,: morsus phalangiorum, (Jahn, restinguit): praecipitationem nimbi,.—
To draw back, unfasten, unclose, open (rare): dentes restringere,to show the teeth,.— Of dogs: rabie restrictā minari,: restrictis forte si labellis riseris, App. poët. Mag. p. 277: restrictis labris,. — Hence, rēstrictus, a, um, P. a. (acc. to I.), bound fast, bound up, tight, close.
Lit.: togis neque restrictis neque fusis,: alvus,i. e. costive,.— Comp.. restrictiores digiti (pedum), i. e. shorter, .—
Trop.
Close, niggardly, stingy (cf.: parcus, tenax): in aliquo esse restrictus,; ; .— Comp., .—
Moderate, modest: an restrictius arbitraris per orbem terrarum legendum dare memoriam suam, quam, etc.,.—
Strict, stern, rigorous, severe, stringent: summum imperium non restrictum nec perseverum volunt,.—Comp.: judicatio,.— Sup.: restrictissimis regulis, Cod. 1, 17 (2), 10.— Adv.: rēstrictē.
Closely, sparingly: facere (with parce),: vivere,. — Comp.: restrictius uti rebus praetereuntibus,.— Sup.: restrictissime facere (opp. plenissime),.—
Strictly, exactly, precisely: cetera non tam restricte praefinio,: restricte tenent illud nomen (sapientium),: observare, ne plus reddat quam acceperit,. — Sup. of the adj. prob. not found.

la:verb:reservo#2.html:
rĕ-servo, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.,
to keep back, save up, qs. for future use; to reserve (very freq. and class.; cf. repono); constr.: aliquid (aliquem) ad aliquid, in aliquid, alicui, with a terminal adv. or absol.
With ad: reliquas merces commeatusque ad obsidionem urbis,: philosophorum libros sibi ad Tusculani requiem atque otium,; : aliquid ad testes,: vitam suam ad incertissimam spem,: hoc consilium ad extremum,: ad ejus periculum legiones,: consulem non ad vitam suam sed ad salutem vestram,: te ad aliquod severius judicium, id. Or. in Tog. Cand. (tom. ii. 1, p. 523 Orell.): vos ad eam rem,: testem ad extremum,: nonne et hominem ipsum ad dubia rei publicae tempora reservandum?(15, 32): utinam ad illa tempora me fortuna reservavisset!: se ad majora,.—
With in: inimicitiasque in aliud tempus reservare,: poenas praesentis fraudis in diem,: partem (stercoris) in pratum,: aliquem in aliud tempus,; : aliquos in unum pugnae laborem,.—
With dat.: natura reservans semina rebus,: illorum esse praedam atque illis reservari,: causam a judicibus praetermissam ipsis (decemviris),: scientiam rei mihi,: tibi se peritura Pergama,: cetera praesenti sermoni,; : ista judicia melioribus meis rebus,: se temporibus aliis,: me Minucio et Salvio,: nos reipublicae,: te non urbi sed carceri,: cui te exitio,: incolumem Pallanta mihi si fata reservant,: se judiciis posterorum,: supplicia alicui,.— *
With a terminal adv.: quid hoc homine facias? aut quo civem importunum reserves?.—(ε) With a simple object, to keep from perishing, to save, preserve (very rare): vide ne, cum velis revocare tempus omnium reservandorum, cum qui servetur non erit, non possis, Orell. N. cr.; cf.: partum reservare,: reservatis Haeduis atque Arvernis,: hominem,: gladiatores,: quaesitique tenax et qui quaesita reservent,.

la:verb:resilio.html:
rĕ-sĭlĭo, ŭi (resiliit, Quadrig. ap. P.;
resilivi,), 4, v. n., to leap or spring back (rare but class.).
Lit.: (exit in terram) in Indiae fluminibus certum genus piscium, ac deinde resilit,: recedere sensim datur (oratoribus): Quidam et resiliunt, quod est plane ridiculum,: (ranae) saepe In gelidos resilire lacus,: piratae in aquas suas,: velites ad manipulos,: a taetro veneno,: polypus ab odore cunilae,; .—
Transf., of things as subjects, to spring back, start back, rebound, recoil, retreat, : juvenis ferit ora sarissā. Non secus haec resilit, quam tecti a culmine grando,: ignis ab ictu,: (cervices) ab imposito nuper jugo,: resilire guttas,: radii infracti,: vulvae tactu,: (Taurus mons) resilit ad Septentriones,retreats, recedes,: in spatium resilire manus breve vidit,to shrink, contract,; cf.: (mamma) detracto alumno suo sterilescit ilice ac resilit,. —
Trop., to recoil, start back, shrink from: ubi scopulum offendis ejusmodi ut ab hoc crimen resilire videas,: instandum iis, quae placere intellexeris, resiliendum ab iis, quae non recipientur,: ut liceret resilire emptori, meliore conditione allatā,to withdraw, recede,.
